items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: Then I taught, I taught music at the Grunewald School of Music.

ctx.x: Then I taught, I taught music at the Grunewald School of Music. Oh, Grunewald, okay. That was a school on Camp Street, around Camp and Julia. I taught trumpet over there and taught a harmony. See because the whole while I was in the Navy I did a lot of studying, studying music.
How was, who supported Grunewald? Was it, wasn't it, was it a government program? Yeah. And GI Bill? Yeah.

And guys went on the GI Bill. See the guys who were married, who went to school there, they would get a check every month for ninety dollars. And with like a ninety dollars a month was a lot of money. Some of the guys didn't, they would play a little jobs. Right. But they would, the thing where they really made the income was from going to school. And it was a very good school, they had some good material. Some of the guys didn't go there to learn.
